      Humans of Harker: Timing turns the tide

      by Sam Li, Humans of Harker Managing Editor

      Six games, one final prediction

      Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream face off in WNBA finals
      by Liana Barooah, Sports and Photo Editor
      October 28, 2026
      Categories:
      • Podcasts
      • Sports

      Listen along as Sports and Photo editor Liana Barooah (11) shares her predictions for the game six of the WNBA finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream.

      harkeraquila · Six games, one final prediction

      Liana Barooah, Sports and Photo Editor: Hi, I’m Liana and I’m the sports and photo editor for Harker Aquila and today I’m going to  be talking about my predictions for game six of the WNBA finals, which will be between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream tomorrow at 9:30 a.m.

      Looking ahead to game 6, I’m leaning towards the Golden State Valkyries to close out the series and win the championship in six games. However, the Atlanta Dream has the home court advantage, which is another aspect to factor in.

      One of the biggest change makers will be Valkyries center Kiah Stokes who put up 13 points, 8 rebounds and three blocks in game 5. Her presence especially in the paint on defense could be crucial yet again, especially if Atlanta tries to weave through defenders and aim to attack the basket. However, on the dream’s side, I’m expecting forward Angel Reese to come back hot after a very inefficient game 5 as her field goal percentage was 25%. If she can control the rebounds like normal and convert more of her close range opportunities, Atlanta does have a chance to force a game 7 for the series

      I’m also expecting Valkyries forward Gabby Williams to continue scoring above her regular-season average of 14.4 points per game. She has averaged nearly 20 points per game in the playoffs, making her a major offensive threat for Golden State. If she can maintain that scoring momentum in Game 6, she could be a deciding factor in helping the Valkyries secure the championship.

      However, my hot take is that Kaitlyn Chen, the Valkyries guard, deserves a much bigger role in this series. She’s made a huge jump from her first season to second one this season and averaged around 7 points a game while shooting efficiently from the field. She might not be the biggest name on the roster, but her ability to knock down field goals off quick passes makes her a valuable option directly off the bench. I think Golden State could benefit from giving her more opportunities to provide an offensive spark for the team, especially if the starters start to get fatigued after high energy play. 

      The pressure will be completely different from a regular season game because one mistake could determine the outcome of the series. I’m expecting both teams to lean heavily on their most reliable players, and whoever executes better under the pressure will come out on top. 

      Overall, Thursday’s game will be incredibly close and I wouldn’t be surprised if it came down to the final few seconds. This is a deciding game for Atlanta, which is fighting to keep the championship hopes alive while Golden State also has the chance to make literal history by winning the title in their second season. With that much on the line for both sides, every possession makes a difference.
